I find them unworthy."
"You left out duplicitous and sniveling.|Darth Maul and Darth Sidious|"[[Darth Maul: Saboteur]]"}} '''Neimoidians''', also known as '''Neimoidian Duros''', were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] that were distant genetic relatives of [[Duros/Legends|Duros]]. They were native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]] and also lived on [[Purse world/Legends|colony worlds]] in the same sector like [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], [[Deko Neimoidia/Legends|Deko Neimoidia]], and [[Koru Neimoidia/Legends|Koru Neimoidia]]. Neimoidians placed tremendous value on wealth and material possessions, and would go to great lengths to gain [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|money]] and power, resulting in a stereotype of being greedy and cowardly; however, they were very easily intimidated, and hated combat. In the years prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Neimoidians became infamous for running the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], a massive corporate entity. Famous Neimoidians included [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] and [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]], high ranking members of the Trade Federation who later joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a separatist movement which waged [[Clone Wars/Legends|war]] on the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. This proved to be their species' undoing: Neimoidia and its colonies were [[Battle on Neimoidia/Legends|blockaded and invaded]] by the Republic in the war's [[19 BBY/Legends|final year]], destroying many Neimoidian [[Grub-hatchery|grub-hatcheries]] and catastrophically affected the long-term survival of the species. Thereafter, the Neimoidians faded from prominence in galactic affairs.''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' ==Biology and appearance== {{Quote|The Neimoidians, especially, are cowards in any theater other than commerce.|Palpatine|''[[Cloak of Deception]]''}} [[File:GoldTapestryNeimoidian-SSbts.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A Neimoidian female]] Since the Neimoidians were distant genetic relatives of the Duros, they retained many similarities to them, including basic form, noseless faces, and green-blue skin (though Neimoidians tended to be grayer, and in some cases like [[Mar Tuuk/Legends|Mar Tuuk]]; even yellow). Their eyes also had pupils that split horizontally, and they were distinguished by small lumps on their foreheads and down-turned mouths. Their sense of smell came from glands under their eyes. These genetic differences were attributed to the distinct features of their homeworld, Neimoidia, including its gravity, which was heavier than [[Duro/Legends|Duro]]. Additionally, the planet's star was dimmer, and the planet itself was humid and widely shrouded by fog and mist. Neimoidian skin often took on a mottled look if the being was too self-indulgent or often prone to great stress, such as [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]]. A Neimoidian's lung pods would expand and contract convulsively under great stress, leading to an old saying characterizing Neimoidians as the only sentient species with an entire organ devoted to worrying. Nauseated Neimoidians' skin turned pink. The Neimoidians had five fingers and two clawlike toes. Neimoidians were born in a larval state called a "grub" form. Although hive-mothers had cloacas, the grubs were born live and not from eggs.''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]'' Many Duros took great offense at being compared to their Neimoidians cousins. In the [[TriPlanetary Press/Legends|TriPlanetary Press]] reference source known as the ''[[Encyclopedia Galactica]]'', the entry for Neimoidian read, "''See: Duros''".{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|regional/13228_2.html|Duros Dispute Encyclopedia}} The classic example of what ''not'' to say detailed an employer for a shipping company who was curious as to why a Neimoidian would be applying for a pilot's position when it was, in actuality, a Duros. The reason for the offense is obvious: Neimoidians tended to be cowardly, greedy, and fearful of death, while Duros were an adventurous, gregarious, and peaceful race. It is well-known that Neimoidians were notorious disease carriers. According to a joke made by [[Ebenn Q3 Baobab/Legends|Ebenn Q3 Baobab]], onetime doctor for a Neimoidian fleet, "the principal export of the Neimoidian home planet is [[Brainworm Rot Type C]]". Baobab further explained in his [[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']] that both the [[Great Pandemic of Deersheba]] and the [[Intestinal Revenge of Bars Barka]] (which emaciated scores of [[Ubese/Legends|Ubese]] colonists) originated with the Neimoidians.[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']] At several times in the past, Neimoidia had been quarantined and forbidden to travelers. [[File:LottDodBD3000droids-SenateSpy.png|thumb|right|220px|Senator Lott Dod with [[BD-3000 luxury droid/Legends|BettyBot]] attendants]] Upon death, Neimoidian bodies would desiccate rapidly if not immediately buried or burned. The corpse's face would elongate, and the brain sac would shrivel into a series of tiny pods behind the head.''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]'' Many Neimoidians believed that it was this terrifying image of death that inspired the appearance of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]],''[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace: The Expanded Visual Dictionary]]'' but in fact the B1-Series battle droids were modeled after their [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]]''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' designers and builders. Whenever they laughed, their head remained the same, but their body shook ever so slightly.''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'' ==Society and culture== ===Education and early life=== {{Quote|I realize that your voracious desires stem from the cruel conditions of your upbringing—you and your fellow grubs in ruthless competition for limited supplies of fungus. But I understand. We are all shaped by our infantile desires, our longing for affection and attention, our fears of death. And judging by how far you have come, it's clear that you were unrivaled and continue to be.|Darth Sidious, to Nute Gunray|[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]}} Neimoidians spent their formative [[Standard year/Legends|years]] as puny grubs in the [[Neimoidian communal hive|communal hives]] of Neimoidia, until the age of seven standard years. They were knowingly neglected by being given limited amounts of food. In this way, the weaker individuals were weeded while the most acquisitive ones could hoard more food than they could eat by themselves. The Neimoidian education ensured the survival of the greediest. Because of that, the Neimoidians would retain ill memories of their homeworld and tried to avoid it as much as possible. In fact, Neimoidia's most able individuals typically left the planet at a young age, often joining the Trade Federation and its trading starships. Meanwhile, the weakest and least capable of the species were sequestered on Neimoidia and the purse-worlds, where they tended to vast insect hives, fungus farms, and beetle hatcheries. In large part because of their formative years and communal hives, the Neimoidians tended to place positions such as [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]] as absolute and obey them without question, nor could they even make independent decisions. As such, if the Viceroy was killed, incapacitated, or otherwise indisposed during a conflict, the Neimoidians will be unable to continue fighting. This trait was notably exploited during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] by [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] to ensure a quick and decisive end to the crisis.[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]] Similarly, the Neimoidians because of their upbringing requiring them to be materialistic, they also placed particular emphasis on one's status. This even extended to the number of [[Blast door/Legends|blast doors]] aboard Neimoidian ships, with three blast doors indicating that the ones behind the blast doors were of high-level in Neimoidian society and thus superior.[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] ===Matters of business=== {{Quote|Look, money is important, sure, but if money was all we were after, we'd be Neimoidians.|Vilmarh Grahrk|[[Star Wars (1998) 41|''Star Wars'' (1998) 41]]}} As adults, Neimoidians had a reputation of being skilled in matters of business and were well known for their leadership of the Trade Federation. Unfortunately, Neimoidians were stereotyped by other species as greedy, fearful of death, lazy, corrupt and even child neglecters. This was evident by the use of [[Droid/Legends|droids]] for almost everything. It was often said that one of the most difficult concepts for a Neimoidian to understand was loyalty. Members of other species often perceived the Neimoidians as villainous. In fact, the notions of morality and ethics that motivated other societies were completely absent from the Neimoidian culture. From infancy, they were reared to believe that anything they could appropriate was theirs by right, regardless of the means used.''[[Secrets of Naboo]]'' Their species was noted for being highly fearful to fight their own battles yet were deceitful to the point that they did not trust living soldiers. Such traits meant that they were often criticized for their cowardly nature and was one of the reasons why they made use of a mechanized army consisting of droids.''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]'' In addition, the discussion of an individual's feelings was considered an anaethema amongst Neimoidians. Although they possessed the reputation of being cowardly and deceitful, the Neimoidians when push comes to shove showed surprising ferocity and tenacity when defending their purse worlds, which was best demonstrated with the [[Neimoidian Home Defense Legion/Legends|Neimoidian Home Defense Legions]] within the Confederacy of Independent Systems.{{InsiderCite|71|CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 14:10:05 Edition}} The Empire's seizure of most Neimoidian assets after the Clone Wars, coupled with the destruction of many grub-hatcheries during that conflict, forced significant social change. Some Neimoidian worlds began to reconsider the values instilled by their harsh upbringing, shifting away from selfishness and rampant indulgence toward a more modest and evenly structured system. Some skeptics maintained that this transformation was only the result of diminished resources rather than genuine reform. Nevertheless, a new generation of Neimoidians was raised with cultural values distinct from their forebears, tempering—though never erasing—the acquisitive instincts of their past.[[Desperate Allies|''Desperate Allies'']] ===Clothing=== [[File:Maul_Neimoidians.png|thumb|left|200px|[[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] Gunray with two [[Aide/Legends|aides]] and [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].]] Because of their obsession with status, the Neimoidians placed great importance in clothing. Among their kind, elaborate clothes were specifically designed to assert an individual's personal wealth and rank and also to instil jealousy or envy in others. Not only did their robes, cloaks, hats and collars all have particular symbolic meanings, but so did their fabrics and colors. The Human [[Rella]] once joked that a Neimoidian would never spend some of their profits unless they could spend it on new robes. Ranks and garments were so closely associated that a Neimoidian disgraced by their peers would be stripped of their clothes immediately. They were particularly attached to their hats, and a popular opinion was that a Neimoidian would never be seen without it unless they were dead.''[[Boba Fett: Hunted]]'' That may not have been true for all historical eras, however, as bare-headed Neimoidians would frequently be spotted during the [[Galactic War]]. The numerous types of Neimoidian headgear ranged from simple caps that revealed the complete forehead[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']] to a wide variety of miters and crowns, some of which even comprised [[Wig/Legends|wig]]-like ornaments.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode204.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Senate Spy}} In fact, the Neimoidian clothing etiquette was so complex that the [[Republic Xenosociological Database]] contained a whole subdirectory pertaining to that subject. ===Language=== The native language of the Neimoidians was called the [[Pak Pak/Legends|Pak Pak]]. That term actually referred to both a verbal language and a nonverbal way of communication that consisted in complex hand gestures. To non-Neimoidians, the verbal Pak Pak sounded like a string of guttural croaks that had a certain musical quality. While most Neimoidians were able to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], they did it with a heavy accent.{{Film|I}} ==History== {{Quote|Neimoidians are the only sentient species with an entire organ devoted solely to the task of worrying.|Old saying|}} [[File:Lok_Durd.png|thumb|right|150px|An extremely corpulent Neimoidian, [[Lok Durd/Legends|Lok Durd]]]] In [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]], a Duros colony was established on Neimoidia under the leadership of [[Chla C'cHaan]].{{GamerCite|2|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Duros}} Due to the distinct features of Neimoidia, including a gravity which was greater than Duro, the Duros colonists became a separate species from their genetic cousins, thus starting the Neimoidian species. During an expansionist period in the [[Old Republic era]], the Neimoidians colonized several nearby worlds. The wealthiest and most resource-rich colony worlds were known as "purse worlds", that also served as administrative posts and ruled their own set of colonies. Notable purse worlds included [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], [[Deko Neimoidia/Legends|Deko Neimoidia]], and [[Koru Neimoidia/Legends|Koru Neimoidia]] . In [[350 BBY/Legends|350 BBY]], the Neimoidians helped establish the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], an association of business and trade groups which grew to dominate entire star systems.[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']] In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] had all the non-Neimoidian members of the [[Trade Federation Directorate]] murdered at the [[Eriadu Trade Summit|Eriadu Conference]]. As a result, the Neimoidians assumed complete control of the Federation. Despite centuries of running the Trade Federation, their control began to subside when the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] began taxation of the trade routes that they had established. This act destroyed the Neimoidians along with their delicate financial control over the Trade Federation which began to crumble as a result. The institution of taxes on trade routes to the outlying regions left the Neimoidians furious. This resulted in the Trade Federation's [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]]. However, the Trade Federation forces were defeated during the battle of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. From this event, most of the stereotype regarding Neimoidians as greedy, conniving cowards was gained. Their humiliating defeat during the trade blockade of Naboo left the Neimoidian reputation entering into a downward spiral. After being bereft of position and power, they began considering every possibility in order to regain their status. [[File:Gilramos.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] and [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]] with Neimoidian soldiers.]] During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], the Neimoidians aligned themselves with [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] growing [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist movement]]. With the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] at the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Neimoidians became a species commonly associated with the Confederacy and were usually either deported from or prevented from entering [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. In addition, Neimoidian warriors and brutes were used in the [[Confederacy military/Legends|Separatist armed forces]] as a part of [[Neimoidian Gunnery Battalion]]. In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Republic retook Neimoidia and its purse worlds from the Confederacy before [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] Gunray and [[Settlement Officer/Legends|Settlement Officer]] [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]] were killed at [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. During the [[Battle on Neimoidia/Legends|assault on Neimoidia]], the planet was ravaged, and the destruction of many Neimoidian [[Grub-hatchery|grub-hatcheries]] would affect the Neimoidian species.''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]'' Under the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Trade Federation was disbanded after Acting Viceroy [[Sentepeth Findos]] [[Imperial–Trade Federation treaty|signed a treaty]] on Neimoidia that gave [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] control of the Trade Federation's assets.{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}} Neimoidians then began adopting the culture of the baseline Duros to disassociate themselves with the Trade Federation's shameful legacy, something no doubt encouraged by the book ''[[Encyclical on Historical Greatness]]'' written by influential Neimoidian [[Chal Haan]]. The Duros, of course, vehemently denied this, as it was considered a great insult to be associated in any way with their genetic cousins. By the time of the rise of the New Republic, however, the Duros were friendlier towards the Neimoidians, and respected their business skills. Some Neimoidians joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]; however, they often faced difficulties, as many members associated their species with the Trade Federation and its role in the rise of the Empire. Others regarded them as potential allies motivated by lingering Separatist grievances, though longstanding stereotypes continued to shape perceptions. Those who did join the Alliance typically did so independently, without allowing others to define their identity. [[File:CotG_Ep_II_Chasing_Ghosts.png|thumb|right|250px|[[Lor Keln]] pulls a blaster on a foe.]] Fewer Neimoidians also traveled far from their homeworlds, although their vehicles and weaponry—such as [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle/Legends|''Sheathipede''-class transport shuttles]], [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|''Vulture'' droids]], and [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleships]] and [[Core ship/Legends|core ships]]—were often used by various corporate entities, particularly in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]]. Neimoidians were known by most denizens of the galaxy as being notorious virus carriers, responsible for such diseases as the [[Great Pandemic of Deersheba]] and the [[Intestinal Revenge of Bars Barka]], with many claiming that the chief export of Neimoidia was [[Brainworm Rot Type C]]. This history of reported disease cases grew so virulent that by [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]], Neimoidia was officially quarantined and declared off limits to all travelers. During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], some Neimoidians joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] as pilots. Many others fell in with criminal organizations as well. One known [[Unidentified Neimoidian Sith|Neimoidian]] was a member of [[One Sith]] during the [[Legacy era]], tasked with guarding the [[Chambers of Persuasion]] in [[XoXaan's Temple]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].[[Legacy (2006) 49|''Legacy'' (2006) 49]] ===Neimoidians in the galaxy=== Around five hundred years before the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], Neimoidian traders sold a decommissioned [[Hoersch-Kessel Drive, Inc./Legends|Hoersch-Kessel]] [[LH-3010 capital freighter]] to [[Hugo Bartyn]], who used it to build his own city in [[Lamaredd/Legends|Lamaredd]]. Five centuries later, Bartyn's descendant [[Guther Bartyn|Guther]] welcomed the visit of a Neimoidian dignitary and competed with him in a global race.{{GamerCite|7|Bartyn's Landing (article)}} ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Bts_bg.jpg|thumb|left|200xp|Early concept art of a Neimoidian]] Though the etymology of the Neimoidian name is unclear, their original designation "S'hatnarian" was explained by [[George Lucas]] in the cut segments of the 2007 interview by [[Wikipedia:Seth MacFarlane|Seth MacFarlane]], featured on the Region 2 [[Wikipedia:It's a Trap!|Family Guy: It's a Trap!]] DVD. During the troubled filming of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], Lucas frequented a bar not far from [[Industrial Light & Magic]] in the Presidio of San Francisco named "Hombres" (now "La Terrasse"). There he met, and would regularly meet [[Wikipedia:William Shatner|William Shatner]], who was living in San Francisco at the time doing stage work. The two became good friends and, as Lucas explained ''Star Wars'', Shatner joked "You'll have to name a character after me." George nodded and agreed, but never followed through. Upon restarting the ''Star Wars'' franchise with ''Episode I'', he considered "S'hatnarian" as a title for the Neimoidians, only to drop the name later.[[Wikipedia:It's a Trap!|Family Guy: It's A Trap!]] Region 2 DVD Easter Egg - Cutting Room Floor, Scraps from the Blue Harvest Interview It is possible, however, that George Lucas instead named the Neimoidians after fellow actor [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Nimoy Leonard Nimoy], who co-starred with Shatner in ''[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Trek:_The_Original_Series Star Trek]''. Early Neimoidian designs portrayed them as a thin-faced species, intending for the [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] to mimic their appearance. When this design was dropped, they were given a new look based on that of the Duros. In the process, they went from computer-generated characters to actors wearing animatronic masks. The original design was eventually modified to become the Geonosians, thus preserving the idea that the battle droids resembled their makers.{{DB|species|geonosian|Geonosian}} The intended association between the appearance of battle droids and the Neimoidians was not dropped, though, as ''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]'' and [[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']] stated that the droids were based on Neimoidian skeletons. ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'' [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] this claim into a belief held by "the fearful Neimoidians."''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'' ''[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace: The Expanded Visual Dictionary]]'' described this claim as a belief held by "many Neimoidians" and ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' explained that this claim is a false rumor spread by "Neimoidian crewers." Much as [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] were given [[Wikipedia:English people|English]] accents, [[Silas Carson]], who portrayed [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], was asked to imitate a [[Wikipedia:Thai language|Thai]] actor's reading of his lines when looping Nute Gunray's dialog for the movie.{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/profile/f20020530/index.html|text=Silas Carson: Hero with a Thousand Faces}} The use of [[wikipedia:Thai|Thai]] accents to depict the Neimoidians was cited by reviewers as part of a broader issue with racial stereotypes in that film."[http://www.usnews.com/usnews/opinion/articles/990712/archive_001413.htm Fu Manchu on Naboo]," ''[http://www.usnews.com
